steps.say: The spine is read as three vertical pillars, and the middle one decides stability. When the back wall of the body bursts backward into the canal, the burst threatens the canal and is potentially unstable. That backward fragment is what threatens the cord.
steps.tx: The **Denis columns** (three-pillar spine model) split anterior, middle and posterior columns into **3** (three) parts. Middle-column failure with **retropulsion** (backward bone fragment) defines the unstable **burst fracture** (exploded vertebral body) that threatens the canal, since the posterior wall fragment sits against the cord itself.

steps.say: A point score built from the scan shape, the ligament damage and the nerve examination decides brace versus operation. Low scores are braced, high scores are fixed. The middle zone is decided case by case with the patient involved.
steps.tx: **TLICS** (thoracolumbar injury score) sums **morphology** (break shape: compression **1** (one), burst **2** (two), translation-rotation **3** (three), distraction **4** (four)) plus **posterior ligamentous complex** (rear tension band) and neurology points. Totals of **5 or more** (five or above) favour surgery while **3 or less** (three or below) favour bracing, with 4 decided individually.

steps.say: A burst that leaves the nerves untouched and the rear ligaments intact heals well in a brace that bends the spine backward. But a worsening deficit, a locked joint or an open wound changes everything. Those cases go urgently to decompression and metalwork.
steps.tx: A burst fracture with intact neurology and no posterior ligament injury is braced in **hyperextension** (backward-bending support), while progressive deficit, locked **facet dislocation** (jammed small joint) or open injury goes for urgent **decompression** (canal freeing) and fixation. Intact nerves plus intact ligaments mark the braceable burst; either failing moves the case toward surgery.

steps.say: Seat belts save lives but are the cause of horizontal splits of the spine in a crash. When only bone is cracked, a brace heals it; when the rear ligaments are torn, only a metal tension band holds. The scan tells bone from ligament injury.
steps.tx: **Chance fractures** (seat-belt split injuries) divide the vertebra horizontally, with bony **Chance** (bone-only split) healing in a brace and ligamentous Chance needing posterior **tension-band** (rear metal strap) fixation. The **seat-belt** (lap-strap mechanism) history plus MRI ligament signal separates the braceable crack from the tear needing metal.

steps.say: A fused bamboo spine snaps like chalk after even a trivial fall, and the break runs through all three pillars. Short screws are pulled straight out of soft bone, so surgeons are spanning long lengths above and below. Every minor fall in these patients deserves a full spine scan.
steps.tx: **Ankylosing spondylitis** (fused bamboo spine) and DISH spines snap as **chalk-stick fractures** (clean transverse breaks) even after minor falls. **Long-segment fixation** (multi-level metal bridging) is needed because short constructs pull out of osteoporotic bone, and missed breaks displace catastrophically, so scan the whole spine after any fall.

steps.say: Crushed vertebrae in thin-boned elderly patients usually heal without an operation. Painkillers, a brace and bone-strengthening drugs carry most through, and cement injections are reserved for fractures that stay painfully unhealed. Operating on every crush would harm more than help.
steps.tx: **Osteoporotic fractures** (thin-bone crushes) without neurology are managed with analgesia, bracing and osteoporosis treatment. **Vertebroplasty** (cement injection) or **kyphoplasty** (balloon plus cement) is reserved for persistently painful non-healing fractures, since routine cementing adds leak and adjacent-break risk without better healing.

steps.say: No steroids for cord injury, careful rolling to protect alignment, and early surgery for unstable patterns. Fixing within three days cuts chest infections and clots from lying in bed. Pressure care and clot prevention run alongside from day one.
steps.tx: No steroids for cord injury: **log-rolling** (spine-kept-straight turns), **pressure care** (skin protection) and **early fixation** (surgery within **72 hours** (seventy two hours)) for unstable patterns cut chest and clot problems from long lying in bed. Chemical clot prophylaxis joins once bleeding settles, completing the bed-rest complication bundle.

steps.say: A healed fracture that slowly bends forward past thirty degrees, aches constantly or wakes new weakness needs late correction. Surgeons cut a wedge from the back and straighten the spine onto rods. Small painless bends are simply watched.
steps.tx: **Post-traumatic kyphosis** (forward bend after fracture) above **30 degrees** (thirty degrees) with lasting ache, or a **delayed deficit** (new late weakness) once the fracture has healed, earns late wedge-cut **osteotomy** (bone straightening cut) with rods and fusion. Cord draping over the bend explains the new weakness, converting a cosmetic hump into a surgical problem.
